problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $3\times 3$ identity matrix after applying the row operations ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2}?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times  \\ B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =I\,✓ \\ C & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ only".
